```{r cars}
data <- read.csv("InFORM_FireOccurrence_Public_-904755089098175112.csv")
#https://data-nifc.opendata.arcgis.com/datasets/60a94840152b4a89bec467a9f052f135_0/explore?filters=eyJQT09TdGF0ZSI6WyJVUy1JRCJdLCJGaXJlRGlzY292ZXJ5RGF0ZVRpbWUiOlsxNDk2MjkzMjAwMDAwLDE3MzAzNTA4MDAwMDBdLCJQT09Db3VudHkiOlsiQWRhIiwiQ2FueW9uIl19&location=16.048663%2C-12.599097%2C1&showTable=true

weather <- read.csv("4419504.csv")
#https://www.ncdc.noaa.gov/cdo-web/confirmation


nrow(data)
nrow(weather)
head(weather)
head(data)

#cleaning the wildfire data

#only wildfires aka not human started
wf <- data |> filter(Incident.Type.Category == "WF") |>
  mutate(DATE = as.Date(parse_date_time(Fire.Discovery.Date.Time, "mdY IMS p")))

#columns that are desired
wf <- wf |> select(POO.County, POO.State, Incident.Name, Incident.Type.Category, Incident.Size, Initial.Latitude, Initial.Longitude, FireOutDateTime, DATE )
#filter for jun - oct as that is when wildfire are typically
wf <- wf |> filter(month(DATE) %in% 6:10)
#combine multiple fires on the same day
wf <- wf |> 
  group_by(DATE) |> 
  summarise(
    POO.County = paste(unique(POO.County), collapse = ", "),
    POO.State = paste(unique(POO.State), collapse = ", "),
    Incident.Name = paste(Incident.Name, collapse = ", "),
    Initial.Latitude = paste(unique(Initial.Latitude), collapse = ", "),
    Initial.Longitude = paste(unique(Initial.Longitude), collapse = ", "),
    Incident.Type.Category = paste(unique(Incident.Type.Category), collapse = ", "),
    Incident.Size = paste(unique(Incident.Size), collapse = ", "),
    FireOutDateTime= paste(unique(FireOutDateTime), collapse = ", "),
    Number_of_Fires = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
View(wf)


#cleaning the weather data
climate <- weather |> select(-TAVG)
climate <- climate |> 
  mutate(DATE = as.Date(DATE))
head(climate)

#combine the two datasets

combined_data <- climate |> 
  left_join(wf, by = "DATE")
combined_data <- combined_data |> 
  mutate(
    Number_of_Fires = ifelse(is.na(Number_of_Fires), 0, Number_of_Fires),
    Fire = ifelse(Number_of_Fires > 0, 1, 0)
  )


view(combined_data)

training <- combined_data |> 
  filter(format(DATE, "%Y") <= 2021)
validation <- combined_data |> 
  filter(format(DATE, "%Y") %in% c("2022", "2023"))
testing <- combined_data |> 
  filter(format(DATE, "%Y") == 2024)
View(training)
View(testing)
View(validation)

colnames(training)



```

```{r}
#Logistic Regression
#source: https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/r-language/logistic-regression-in-r-programming/


model <- glm(
  Fire ~ PRCP + AWND + TMIN,
  data = training,
  family = binomial()
)

valid <- predict(model,
                newdata = validation, 
                type = "response")
valid <- ifelse(
  valid >= 0.5,
  1,
  0
)

#a matrix
matrix <- table(
  Actual = validation$Fire,
  Predicted = valid)
matrix

accuracy <- mean(valid == validation$Fire) * 100
accuracy




#trying to improve the model
model2 <- glm(
  Fire ~ AWND + PRCP + TMAX + TMIN,
  data = training,
  family = binomial()
)
summary(model2)

#Validation Step

#response is used to return probabilities
#probabilties of fires
valid2 <- predict(model2,
                newdata = validation, 
                type = "response")
valid2 <- ifelse(
  valid2 >= 0.5,
  1,
  0
)

#a matrix
matrix2 <- table(
  Actual = validation$Fire,
  Predicted = valid)
matrix2

#accuracy of model2
accuracy2 <- mean(valid2 == validation$Fire) * 100
accuracy2

#fire detection based on matric is 95/(95+75) = 55.9%

testing
test_prob <- predict(
  model2,
  newdata = testing,
  type = "response"
)
test_prob <- ifelse(
  test_prob >= 0.5,
  1,
  0
)
test_matrix <- table(
  Actual = testing$Fire,
  Predicted = test_prob)
test_matrix


```
